title: I'm from Indonesia
title_target: ကျွန်မ အင်ဒိုနီးရှားက လာပါတယ် — cha.ma. iⁿ-doh-nee:-sha:-ga. la-ba-dè
goal: Say where you're from, which languages you speak, and what you do — and get used to Burmese word order, where the verb always comes last.
bekal: say your country and city with …က လာတယ်
say which languages you speak with …စကား ပြောတတ်တယ်
ask about and state someone's job
build sentences with the verb at the end without thinking
use the ending တယ် in statements

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — At the office, first day
dialogs.intro: It's Ani's first day at the office. Daw Khin, the department head, introduces her to Ko Zaw. Watch how every sentence is built: the details first, the object first, and **the verb always last**. Read the literal lines slowly — that's where this unit's lesson is.

lines.speaker: ဒေါ်ခင်:
lines.text: [ကိုဇော်|koh-zò]၊ [ဒါ|da] [အာနီ|a-nee] [ပါ|ba]။ [အင်ဒိုနီးရှား|iⁿ-doh-nee:-sha:] [က|ga.] [လာ|la] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။
lines.id: Ko Zaw, this is Ani. She's from Indonesia.
lines.literal: ko-zaw, this — ani — polite. indonesia — from — come — polite-statement.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [မင်္ဂလာပါ|miⁿ-ga-la-ba]။ [အင်ဒိုနီးရှား|iⁿ-doh-nee:-sha:] [ဘယ်|bè] [မြို့|myoh.] [က|ga.] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.literal: blessing-be. indonesia — which — city — from — Q?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဂျာကာတာ|ja-ka-ta] [က|ga.] [ပါ|ba]။ [ဒါပေမဲ့|da-bay-mè.] [အခု|a.hkoo.] [ရန်ကုန်|yaⁿ-kohⁿ] [မှာ|hma] [နေ|nay] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။
lines.id: From Jakarta. But now I live in Yangon.
lines.literal: jakarta — from — polite. but — now — yangon — in — live — polite-statement.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ဘာ|ba] [အလုပ်|a.lohk] [လုပ်|lohk] [လဲ|lè:]။

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ကျွန်မ|cha.ma.] [အင်ဂျင်နီယာ|iⁿ-jiⁿ-nee-ya] [ပါ|ba]။ [ကိုဇော်|koh-zò] [ရော|yò:]။
lines.id: I'm an engineer. And you, Ko Zaw?
lines.literal: I(f) — engineer — polite. ko-zaw — how about?

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ကျွန်တော်|cha.nò] [ဒီမှာ|dee-hma] [စာရေး|sa-yay:] [လုပ်|lohk] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [ဆယ်|hsay] [နှစ်|hnik] [ရှိ|shee.] [ပြီ|bee]။
lines.id: I'm a clerk here. It's been ten years.
lines.literal: I(m) — here-at — clerk — do — polite-statement. ten — year — exist — already.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဘယ်|bè] [ဘာသာစကား|ba-tha-za.ga:] [တွေ|dway] [ပြော|pyò:] [တတ်|tak] [လဲ|lè:]။

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [မြန်မာစကား|myaⁿ-ma-za.ga:] [နဲ့|nè.] [အင်္ဂလိပ်စကား|iⁿ-ga.layk-sa.ga:] [ပြော|pyò:] [တတ်|tak] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။
lines.literal: myanmar-language — and — english-language — speak — skilled — polite-statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ကျွန်မ|cha.ma.] [အင်္ဂလိပ်စကား|iⁿ-ga.layk-sa.ga:] [ပြော|pyò:] [တတ်|tak] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]၊ [မြန်မာစကား|myaⁿ-ma-za.ga:] [နည်းနည်း|nè:-nè:] [ပဲ|bè:]။
lines.id: I speak English, but only a little Burmese.
lines.literal: I(f) — english-language — speak — skilled — polite-statement, myanmar-language — little — only.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]၊ [ဒါပေမဲ့|da-bay-mè.] [အခု|a.hkoo.] [ကောင်း|kowⁿ:] [နေ|nay] [ပြီ|bee]။ [ဘယ်မှာ|bè-hma] [သင်|thiⁿ] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: Yes, but it's already good now. Where do you study?
lines.literal: true-yes, but — now — good — -ing — already. where-at — learn — Q?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [အိမ်|ayⁿ] [မှာ|hma] [ကိုယ့်ဘာသာ|koh.-ba-tha] [သင်|thiⁿ] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [စာအုပ်|sa-ohk] [နဲ့|nè.] [ပါ|ba]။
lines.id: I teach myself at home. With a book.
lines.literal: home — at — by-oneself — learn — polite-statement. book — with — polite.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [တော်|tò] [လိုက်တာ|laik-ta]! [ကျွန်တော်|cha.nò] [ကူညီ|koo-nyee] [ပါ့မယ်|ba.-mè]။

grammars.title: ⚠️ The verb stands at the END of the sentence
body: This is the biggest change in thinking in the whole book, and it's best to face it now rather than later. English orders a sentence **doer — verb — object**. Burmese orders it **doer — object — verb**, and the verb never moves from the end.

head: English
Burmese order
The sentence
rows: ကျွန်မ လက်ဖက်ရည် သောက်ပါတယ်။
ကျွန်မ ဂျာကာတာက လာပါတယ်။
ကျွန်မ ရန်ကုန်မှာ နေပါတယ်။
ဘာအလုပ် လုပ်လဲ။

after: The fastest drill: take any English sentence, **move the verb to the end**, and say it. "I eat rice" becomes "I rice eat". It sounds like Yoda in the first week; by the third week it sounds normal.
The good news: since the verb is always at the end, you can build everything else in the sentence first and think about the verb last. Burmese speakers do exactly that every day.

grammars.title: …က and …မှာ — prepositions that come after
body: Burmese has no prepositions; it has **postpositions**. The place, origin, or destination comes first, and the marker follows.

head: Marker
Say it
Meaning
Example
rows: ဂျာကာတာက — from Jakarta
ရန်ကုန်မှာ — in Yangon
ရန်ကုန်ကို — to Yangon
စာအုပ်နဲ့ — with a book
ကျွန်မအတွက် — for me

after: ⚠️ Notice that …က is read *ga.*, not *ka.*, when it leans on the word before it. This k → g change is the same kind as ပါ being read *ba*, and it will keep happening throughout the book.

grammars.title: Saying what you do
body: Jobs follow the pattern "I — job — ပါ", with no verb at all. To ask, use ဘာအလုပ် လုပ်လဲ (literally: "what work do Q").

head: Burmese
Say it
English
rows: အင်ဂျင်နီယာ

after: ⚠️ Many job titles have different male and female forms: ဆရာ for a male teacher, ဆရာမ for a female teacher — a bit like English actor/actress, but far more common. The ending မ marks a woman, and you've already met it in ကျွန်မ.

grammars.title: တွေ — marking the plural when it matters
body: Unlike English, Burmese usually **doesn't mark the plural**. စာအုပ် can mean one book or many books, and the listener knows from context. Only when the number really needs stressing do you use တွေ (*dway*).

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: they — people take တို့, not တွေ

after: ⚠️ တွေ is never used once the number is stated. "Three books" is စာအုပ် သုံး အုပ်, not စာအုပ်တွေ သုံး အုပ် — the number already does the job, so the plural marker would be doubled up.

blocks.text: Almost all country names in Burmese are borrowed from English, so you just reread them with Burmese sounds. Language names are formed by adding စကား (*sa.ga:*, "speech") after the country name.

head: Country
Say it
Its language
rows: အင်ဒိုနီးရှားစကား
မြန်မာစကား
ထိုင်းစကား — Thai
မလေးရှားစကား
အင်္ဂလိပ်စကား — English
တရုတ်စကား — Chinese
ဂျပန်စကား — Japanese

blocks.title: ⚠️ ဗမာ and မြန်မာ — two names for one country
items: **မြန်မာ** (*myaⁿ-ma*) is the official name of the country and its people, used in writing and formal speech.
**ဗမာ** (*ba.ma*) is the older, more casual spoken form, and it's the source of the English name "Burma" — and of "Burmese". At home, people use the two words interchangeably.
For the language, people more often say **ဗမာစကား** (*ba.ma-za.ga:*) in everyday conversation, while မြန်မာစကား sounds more formal. This book uses မြန်မာစကား, and you'll hear both in the street.
